0.0.n: Sets the time for the introduction.

0.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic, highlighting what will happen today.

0.4.n: This is the name of a traditional Japanese festival, literally meaning Rooster Market.

0.6.n: Connects the name 酉の市 to the category 日本の行事.

0.7.n: A country name; 日本の describes the event as Japanese.

0.8.n: Links 日本 to 行事, showing that the event belongs to Japanese culture.

0.9.n: Refers to a traditional or customary occasion, here a festival.

0.10.n: Marks the named Japanese event as what the speaker will introduce.

0.11.n: The polite form of 紹介する; here it announces what the speaker will explain next.

1.1.n: This festival name refers back to the event introduced in the previous sentence.

1.3.n: Marks 酉の市 as the topic being discussed.

1.4.n: Shows that the festival happens annually, not just this year.

1.5.n: Combines with 月 to name the eleventh month, November.

1.6.n: After a number, 月 names a calendar month; 11月 is November.

1.7.n: Marks November as the time when the festival takes place.

1.8.n: Polite passive form of 行う: the festival receives the action, and its organizers are not named.

2.0.n: Describes the festival's bustling, cheerful atmosphere.

2.1.n: The linking form of だ after にぎやか, joining this description to the next one.

2.3.n: Refers to the festival's vitality rather than someone's physical health.

2.4.n: Marks 元気 as what there is plenty of.

2.5.n: Describes an abundance of energy; 元気がいっぱい means the festival is full of vitality.

2.6.n: Connects 元気がいっぱい to お祭り so the whole phrase describes the festival.

2.7.n: The prefix お adds a familiar, polite touch to 祭り and is common in everyday speech.

2.8.n: Ends the sentence politely; the festival being described is understood from context.

0.lit: Today, as for, I will introduce a Japanese event called Tori no Ichi.
0.tip: という links a name to a noun: 酉の市という行事 means an event called Tori no Ichi.

1.lit: As for Tori no Ichi, every year in November it is held.
1.tip: 行われます is passive: the sentence tells us when the festival happens without saying who organizes it.

2.lit: It is lively, and is a festival with energy in abundance.
2.tip: で connects にぎやか to another description, letting you say the festival is lively and full of energy.
